config.title: useMemo for Expensive Computation

intro.title: useMemo for Expensive Computation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that calculates and displays the factorial of a number. You will learn how to use the `useMemo` hook to optimize expensive computations by memoizing the result, ensuring the calculation only re-runs when its dependencies change. The main technologies involved are Angular's component system, TypeScript, and the `useMemo` hook from React (adapted for Angular's context). This will help you improve performance in your applications by avoiding unnecessary recalculations.
intro.usecase: In Angular applications, expensive computations frequently appear in data-intensive dashboards where filtering or sorting large datasets triggers performance bottlenecks. For example, financial analytics platforms that recalculate portfolio metrics on every user interaction would benefit from memoizing these calculations. E-commerce product filters that process thousands of items or real-time data visualizations that transform streaming data are practical scenarios where useMemo prevents unnecessary re-renders. This pattern allows developers to optimize component performance while maintaining responsive user interfaces.

objectives: Implement a computed property in an Angular component to handle expensive calculations
Apply the useMemo pattern using Angular's computed signals for performance optimization
Construct a component that conditionally recomputes values based on dependency changes
Configure a computed signal with specific dependencies to prevent unnecessary recalculations
Update component templates to display memoized values from computed signals
Manipulate input data to observe how computed signals respond to dependency updates
Initialize a performance comparison between computed signals and method calls in templates

steps.title: Import Component and OnInit from @angular/core

steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both symbols from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:

import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';

successCriteria: Component and OnInit are imported from '@angular/core'.

steps.instruction: Create the AppComponent class that implements the OnInit interface. Add the @Component decorator above it with an empty template and selector 'app-root'.
steps.hint: Use the class keyword followed by the component name, then implements OnInit. Add the @Component decorator with template: '' and selector: 'app-root'.

import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';

steps.hint: Use TypeScript type annotations. For example: counter: number = 0;
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have typed state properties ready for use in the template and methods.
successCriteria: AppComponent has 'counter: number = 0' and 'expensiveResult: number = 0' properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, define a method named 'expensiveComputation' that returns a number. This method should simulate a heavy calculation by using a loop that runs many iterations.
steps.hint: You can create a method like 'expensiveComputation(): number { ... }' and inside it, use a for loop to perform many calculations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A method named 'expensiveComputation' is added to the AppComponent class that performs a loop-based calculation and returns a number.
successCriteria: The AppComponent class contains a method named 'expensiveComputation' that uses a loop to simulate heavy computation and returns a numeric value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it's named 'expensiveComputation', returns a number, and includes a loop to simulate heavy computation.

steps.title: Implement ngOnInit lifecycle hook
steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnInit method, initialize the counter property to 0 and the expensiveResult property to the result of calling the expensiveComputation method with a starting value (e.g., 1000).
steps.hint: Remember that ngOnInit runs once when the component initializes. Set the initial state values here.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnInit method will set initial values for the component's state properties when the component loads.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method contains initialization code that sets counter to 0 and expensiveResult to the result of expensiveComputation with a starting value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
